items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: Then they had Charlie Jones (PHONETIC) was the other saxophone player and I

ctx.x: There was a good trumpet player in that band by the name of Lloyd Reese (PHONETIC). Excellent. He became a teacher in this area here and he was excellent saxophonist, also an excellent trumpet player and excellent teacher. He went to school to Whittier College and he studied music out in that grouping out there. Then we had a very, very good saxophone section. We had a fellow by the name of Marvin Johnson (PHONETIC), played alto with me and Bumps Meyers (PHONETIC) was a tenor saxophone player. Then they had…

Then Lawrence played -- Lionel Hampton was the drummer in the band and he worked there for many years with us. That's where I first got to be very good friends with Lionel Hampton. That's when he was deriving his style of playing two-finger piano and xylophones, vibraphones, actually, and then when Lionel formed his band in 1941, I formed his band, worked as his music director with him. I rehearsed his band, put it together for him, picked most of its men from this area out here. My brother, (ERNIE) was the lead…
